{{nihongo|'''Yusen Shrine'''|湯泉神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

'''Yusen Shrine''' (とうせんじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Arimachō|Q18700495|qid=Q18700495}}, {{ill|Kita-ku, Kobe|Q1078814|qid=Q1078814|lt=Kita-ku}}, {{ill|Kobe|Q48320|qid=Q48320}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}. It is also read "Onsen Jinja" and may be written {{ill|Onsen Shrines|Q11562963|qid=Q11562963}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha major shrine}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|comment=this used to link to modern system but that one is too overlinked|lt=gōsha|qid=Q134917316}}.

=== History ===
Based on the tale that {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}} discovered Arima Onsen after seeing three {{ill|Crow|Q388450|qid=Q388450|lt=crows}} soaking in red hot water to heal leg injuries, these two deities are enshrined here, and three birds are carved on the haiden. Together with Kumano Kusumi-no-Mikoto, newly worshiped from the era of restoration of Arima Onsen by priest Ninsei beginning in {{ill|1191|Q19738|qid=Q19738}} ({{ill|Kenkyū|Q1193933|qid=Q1193933}} 2), they are called the "Three Guardian Deities."

Because the '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}' records visits by {{ill|Emperor Jomei|Q329761|qid=Q329761}} and {{ill|Emperor Kōtoku|Q317980|qid=Q317980}}, and because it is listed among the 492 major shrines in the early-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, its high prestige in former times can be seen.

Formerly the shrine buildings (built in the mid-{{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, {{ill|Kansei|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131}} 10 / {{ill|1798|Q7823|qid=Q7823}}) stood in the precincts of {{ill|Onsen-ji Temple|Q11562943|qid=Q11562943|lt=Onsen-ji}} at the foot of Mt. === Shrine name ===
Some documents write it as Onsen Shrine, and proposed readings include "tōsen jinja," "tōzen jinja," and "yuno jinja," but today it is generally written "Yusen Shrine" and read "tōsen jinja." In the section for {{ill|Arima district|Q11516836|qid=Q11516836}} of {{ill|Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163}} in the 'Engishiki' Jinmyōchō, it is listed with {{ill|Arima Shrine|Q11516720|qid=Q11516720}} and {{ill|Kuchi Shrine|Q11392062|qid=Q11392062}} as "Yusen Shrine (yuno jinja)" [http://www.arima-onsen.com/facility_info113.html].
